title: Item
description: The saved contents of a thread. Every item has id, type and the optional parent_id, turn_id, created_at and raw.

Item.description: One entry in a thread, told apart by type.

UserMessage.description: A message to the agent from the user (or the app on their behalf).

steered.description: Sent while a turn was running, so it joined that turn instead of starting one.

queued.description: Sent, but the harness hasn't taken it in yet. An item.updated clears it once it has.

client_id.description: The client_id of the send command that made it, so a client can match it to what it showed while waiting.

parent_id.description: The id of the subagent tool_call this item belongs to. Absent for the main conversation.

turn_id.description: The turn the item was made in.

raw.description: The harness's own payload this came from, for debugging. Backends can leave it out; clients mustn't depend on it.

AssistantMessage.description: Text from the agent. While it streams, delta events append to text; an item.updated sets the final text.

parent_id.description: The id of the subagent tool_call this item belongs to. Absent for the main conversation.

turn_id.description: The turn the item was made in.

raw.description: The harness's own payload this came from, for debugging. Backends can leave it out; clients mustn't depend on it.

Reasoning.description: The agent's thinking, or a summary of it, as the harness gives it. Streams like assistant_message.

parent_id.description: The id of the subagent tool_call this item belongs to. Absent for the main conversation.

turn_id.description: The turn the item was made in.

raw.description: The harness's own payload this came from, for debugging. Backends can leave it out; clients mustn't depend on it.

ToolCall.description: A tool the agent called, with its result once it has one. A subagent is a tool_call of kind subagent: the items it makes have its id as their parent_id. The optional fields after input are the same facts for every harness, set when the kind has them, so a UI can show a call without knowing the harness's tool names.

id.description: The harness's id for the call (Claude's tool_use id, Codex's item id).

name.description: The tool's name as the harness gave it (Bash, Read, apply_patch...). For an MCP tool, the tool's own name; server has the server's.

input.description: The tool's arguments as the harness gave them, usually an object.

title.description: A short summary of the call, e.g. a subagent's description.

path.description: read, search: the file or directory.

query.description: search: the pattern. web: the search query.

todos.description: todo: the whole list after the call.

parent_id.description: The id of the subagent tool_call this item belongs to. Absent for the main conversation.

turn_id.description: The turn the item was made in.

raw.description: The harness's own payload this came from, for debugging. Backends can leave it out; clients mustn't depend on it.

ToolKind.description: What a tool does, for permission policies and for picking a renderer. shell: runs a command. read: reads files. edit: writes or patches files. search: finds files or text (glob, grep). web: fetches or searches the web. mcp: a tool on an external MCP server. app: a tool the app defined. subagent: starts a subagent. todo: updates the agent's plan or todo list. other: anything else.

ToolStatus.description: pending: called, not started (e.g. waiting for permission). running: started, no result yet. completed: it returned. failed: it returned an error. denied: permission was refused. cancelled: the turn ended (e.g. was interrupted) before it returned.

ToolResult.description: What a tool returned. For a failed call, content is the error.

content.description: The result as text. Images become [image].

structured.description: Structured output, when the tool gave some (an app tool's return value, MCP structuredContent).

truncated.description: content was cut short before it was saved.

diff.description: A unified diff of the change, or the content of an added file.

move_to.description: The file's new path, when the change renames it.

Compaction.description: The harness compacted the conversation's context.

parent_id.description: The id of the subagent tool_call this item belongs to. Absent for the main conversation.

turn_id.description: The turn the item was made in.

raw.description: The harness's own payload this came from, for debugging. Backends can leave it out; clients mustn't depend on it.

Notice.description: Something to tell the user that isn't the agent talking: an error, a retry, hook output, a run re-attached after a restart.

code.description: What kind of notice it is, for apps that treat some specially. Known codes: run.reattached (a restarted backend picked up a run that was still going), run.lost (a restarted backend couldn't pick up the run a turn was running in, so the turn ended), retry, hook, stderr.

detail.description: More text, e.g. a stack trace or a hook's full output.

parent_id.description: The id of the subagent tool_call this item belongs to. Absent for the main conversation.

turn_id.description: The turn the item was made in.

raw.description: The harness's own payload this came from, for debugging. Backends can leave it out; clients mustn't depend on it.

TurnResult.description: How a turn ended. The last item of each turn.

ok.description: The turn finished without an error. An interrupted turn isn't ok.

interrupted.description: The turn was stopped by an interrupt command.

parent_id.description: The id of the subagent tool_call this item belongs to. Absent for the main conversation.

turn_id.description: The turn the item was made in.

raw.description: The harness's own payload this came from, for debugging. Backends can leave it out; clients mustn't depend on it.

Attachment.description: A file sent with a message: inline as base64 data, or by path on the backend's machine.
